entities.summary: Pandulf II of Benevento was a prominent ruler in medieval Italy, playing a crucial role in shaping the political landscape of the region. He was the prince of Benevento from 981 and prince of Capua from 1008 or 1009, succeeding his father Landulf III as co-prince between 959 and 968. Pandulf's reign was marked by a series of strategic alliances and military campaigns, which ultimately secured his position as a key player in the politics of southern Italy. Through his relationships with neighboring kingdoms and the Holy Roman Empire, Pandulf II of Benevento left a lasting legacy that continued to influence the region long after his death in 1014. The intricate web of alliances and conflicts that he navigated reveals the complexities of medieval politics and the delicate balance of power in southern Italy during this period. This period of his life was marked by the rise of the Salian dynasty, which would go on to shape the course of Italian history for centuries to come.
